overview_summary: Candidate landing zone located along the elevated northern rim of Faustini crater in the lunar south polar region.
section_geology: The terrain features ancient anorthositic highlands impact breccias with crater wall degradation and mass wasting deposits.
section_history: Evaluated by NASA Artemis III site evaluation team as candidate region with access to permanently shadowed regions.
pro: High proximity to suspected volatile cold traps in permanently shadowed crater floors.
con: Challenging line-of-sight communications during specific orbital phases.

overview_summary: Narrow elevated ridge connecting Shackleton crater to adjacent topographic highs near the lunar South Pole.
section_geology: Anorthositic ridge flank exhibiting multi-ring basin tectonic uplift and shallow regolith overlay.
section_history: Key scientific target for deep-space solar illumination and constant Earth direct line-of-sight communications.
pro: Extended periods of solar illumination exceeding 85% of the lunar annual cycle.
con: Steep local slopes requiring precise terrain-relative navigation for landing hazard avoidance.

overview_summary: Prominent topographic mountain massif standing approximately 5000 meters above surrounding terrain.
section_geology: Pre-Nectarian highland block formed during early South Pole-Aitken basin mega-impact event.
section_history: Extensively studied site offering panoramic direct line-of-sight visibility to Earth and South Pole.
pro: Exceptional continuous direct-to-Earth visibility for high-bandwidth scientific telemetry.
con: High surface roughness and boulder fields along lower approach trajectories.

overview_summary: Broad elevated terrain sector along the northeastern rim perimeter of Amundsen crater.
section_geology: Highland regolith rich in pyroxene and feldspathic materials with impact melt sheet fragments.
section_history: Targeted by robotic reconnaissance for subsurface ice stability models and crater chronology.
pro: Flat local terraces suitable for autonomous lander touchdown footprints.
con: Limited direct solar elevation requiring efficient energy storage during local night.

overview_summary: Highland ridge along the rim crest of Nobile crater adjacent to potential VIPER rover exploration paths.
section_geology: Stratified impact ejecta layers overlying deep crustal anorthosites and ancient basaltic traces.
section_history: Selected for volatile resource prospecting and robotic mobile scout deployment operations.
pro: Close proximity to confirmed surface frost signatures identified by orbital spectroscopy.
con: Variable thermal extremes between illuminated peaks and adjacent deep shadow depressions.
